title: Asynchronous submission reaches success and returns a literal result

source.normalization: Job IDs and timestamps are replaced by template values.

must: Read Location case-insensitively and resolve it against the final response URL.
Expose a job handle and preserve the submission response body and headers.
Allow the caller to request status or use a bounded poll-until-terminal helper.
must_not: Fetch results before a successful terminal status.
Require the initial body status to remain accepted; the server can already report running.

must: Expose status, progress, message, timestamps, links, and unknown fields without requiring all optional fields.
Permit another GET when requested by the caller or polling helper.
must_not: Fetch results while the job is running.
Treat a changed message or non-monotonic optional progress value as a protocol failure.

must: Stop polling after the successful terminal state.
Find the results link by relation, not title or array position, and resolve it against the job response URL.
Keep job completion distinct from whether the result document has already been fetched.
must_not: Continue automatic status polling after a terminal state.
Assume the first link is the results link.

must: Parse the document with the same result parser used for synchronous execution.
Expose Result as the advertised string output and retain the raw response.
must_not: Use a special output model merely because the result was obtained asynchronously.
Discard unknown result IDs if a future server adds them.
